what: exact W=4 board cycles predicted for the L3 board runs of PROTOCOL_2_ADDENDUM.md, written before any of them; per layer CYCLES - IN_STALL must equal "predicted" exactly

protocol.test: a layer is predicted if CYCLES - IN_STALL equals it exactly; every miss is listed

noise: sigma 25 (the manifest's), test_noise seed 0, the board driver's host emulation

board.bitstream: the existing W=4 bitstream (build zed_v4_p16_t4_w4_*), the one of PROTOCOL_2's runs
board.padding: none: every K (36, 288, 324) is a multiple of 4, so no zero taps and, every window being whole beats, no zero windows are added (checked per layer)

core: P = 16 lanes, T = 4 banks, tap t of a window in bank t % 4, sparse mode (mode 1)

rule.count: count_w4 = sum over windows of max(ceil(K/4) + 1, ceil(COUT/16) * max(1, max_b nnz_b), COUT) (denoise/predict_w4.py window_cycles, W = 4, sparse)
rule.fill_drain: conv2..conv10, per board run: min(load, last) + 3 + ((COUT-1) % 16 + 1), load = ceil(K/4) + 1, last = ceil(COUT/16) * max(1, max bank nnz) of the run's last window as the L3 export sends it (denoise/w4_gaps.py); conv1: the measured constant 17 per run

conv1_constant.source: denoise/w4_gaps.json networks["B-32 ReLU + QAT"] conv1 board_w4
conv1_constant.note: measured on the board on 05.png (the Original), not derived; conv1 reads the image, so its windows are the Original's in L3 too (checked); its output rows are relabelled, which changes no window cycle

rule.code: bankperm/predict_board_2.py layer_record and total, imported unchanged (the PROTOCOL_2 rule)

l3.orders_meaning: keyed by producer: order[p] = the original output channel at position p of its map; class p % 4 (fit.order_from_group); a consumer's channel position p of 3x3 position s is sent in slot s*32 + (p + s) % 32 (bank (s + class) % 4) on conv2..conv9
l3.export_command: python bankperm/export_layout.py --layout skew --orders bankperm/perms_2.json --model dn_d10_c32_us_fx_qat --out DIR
l3.no_adapter: export_layout.read_orders reads perms_2.json directly (networks.<label>.orders of the entry with this model) and gives exactly perms_2.json's B-32 ReLU + QAT s1 orders (asserted); the independent mapping below is a second construction of the same export, not an adapter
l3.config_sha256_meaning: SHA-256 of each layer's <layer>_config.bin in the L3 export, the bytes the driver streams as the layer's configuration; identical to the independent rebuild from the original's INT32 words and on every image's record
l3.tap_order_meaning: tap_order[slot] = the folded export's tap index sent in that slot (x_l3 = x_folded[:, order])
l3.platform_note: the config.bin files and manifest.json (export_layout.py writes it with LF) are the same bytes wherever the export is built; int_eval.json is copied from the checkout, so compare it with CRLF read as LF (lf_sha256). permutation_manifest.json (fold.fold: derived_from = str(relative path), written with write_text) has backslashes in derived_from and CRLF line ends when the export is built on Windows, and layout_manifest.json records that file's raw hash: those two do not carry the same hash there and are not what the board streams

assumptions: one board run per layer: every layer here has at most 65536 windows (16,384 on 05-07, 65,536 on 08.png), so run_denoise.py --tile 65536 runs each layer once; with another tile each run pays its own fill/drain

the L3 run is scripts/run_denoise.py --export-dir <the L3 export> on the W=4 bitstream: conv2..conv9 windows with their columns in the export's tap_order (the skew order) after the relabeling folded into the producers, conv1 and conv10 windows as the Original's; the config.bin streamed per layer has the SHA-256 in layouts.l3.config_sha256. A host path that sends other windows or weights is not what is predicted
conv1's fill and drain is the 05.png Original's measured 17 on every image (not a prediction)
CYCLES - IN_STALL is compared; this bitstream's IN_STALL does not count starvation at window boundaries (PROTOCOL_2), so a miss is a miss even with IN_STALL = 0
